editorial:
Peter Rabbit is back, and this time he is feeling misunderstood. After learning that his human family plans to paint him as a troublemaker in their new book, Peter decides to run away and find a place where he can be himself. Along the way, he meets an older, street-smart rabbit named Barnabas who pulls him into a big heist. The movie keeps the same playful energy as the first film, mixing live-action with cute CGI animals and plenty of slapstick humor. You will see Peter struggle between wanting freedom and missing his family, which gives the story a little heart beneath all the chaos.

The voice cast is lively, and the action scenes are bright and fast, making it easy for kids to stay engaged. The humor lands well for both children and adults, though some jokes feel a bit familiar if you watched the first movie. On the downside, the plot can feel rushed, and a few characters do not get enough screen time. Still, if you want a fun family night, this is a solid pick.
endingExplained: In the final act, Peter realizes Barnabas has been using him and his friends for the heist. Peter turns against Barnabas and helps his human family stop the plan. The twist is that Peter's bad reputation in the book actually brings everyone closer together, and he chooses to go home. The movie ends with Peter and his family reunited, showing that being yourself matters more than what others write about you.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies with talking animals.
